findings.what: Case-local promotion backups still act as forgeable provenance and can overwrite registry-bound live artifacts during public restart.
findings.why: The recovery parser treats an original=true applied entry as coherent solely when its case-local backup exists. A portable unsealed case can therefore carry the exact P1 write set with data/sources.json as the applied prefix, original=true, and an attacker-selected regular file at .anomaly/attempts/P1/attempt-1/promotion-backup/data/sources.json; all later entries remain coherent pending originals. The exact-schema, registry-set, producer-order, and whole-tree checks all pass. _rollback then marks the entry rolling_back, discards the live source registry, and executes backup.replace(live), after which cleanup removes the forged journal and backup. The same construction with a full P7 applied prefix can replace README.md and erase journalist content added after the case was received. A regular file inside the untrusted portable case is not independent provenance, so the original=false deletion fix leaves an equally reachable original=true overwrite capability.

findings.what: A producer-reachable interruption after first creating a phase artifact permanently blocks promotion recovery.
findings.why: For a path that did not exist before promotion, _apply durably records status=applying and then moves the staged artifact live before recording status=applied. A process death after that move leaves original=false with a live artifact and either applying or applied status. On every public restart, _validate_recovery_artifacts requires not live.exists() for every non-original non-pending entry, rejects this genuine producer state, and prevents rollback, attempt rewind, and cleanup. P7 normally first-creates findings/findings.json, findings/report.md, findings/charts, and both receipts, so the crash window is reachable on the canonical flow. The recovery tests exercise original=true P1 rollback and forged false provenance, but not this producer-reachable first-creation interruption. This violates AC3 durable atomic promotion and restart-idempotent rollback.

evidence.output: The dynamic-execution hit is ast.literal_eval limited to a quoted scalar and catches SyntaxError/ValueError, not arbitrary eval. PRAGMA interpolation receives only positive non-bool integers from _validate_limits. Prepared table IDs are generated as tbl_ plus a SHA-256 hex digest, and profile rejects anything outside tbl_[0-9a-f]{64}; registered DuckDB views are internal prepared_<integer> names. The five SQL hits therefore have no injection path.

Promotion paths are fixed relative write tuples from the sole owner registry and are exact-schema/producer-order checked. Rollback progress is journalized per entry and original=true partial restores can restart. However line 287 trusts any case-local backup as original provenance, while line 289 rejects every non-original non-pending entry whose promoted live artifact exists, yielding the two blocking provenance/recovery paths reported above.

The hard-exit attempt-count proof reconciles missing failure evidence; the producer-ordered and second-interruption rollback proofs use pre-existing P1 artifacts with original=true; the forged-provenance proof checks original=false/live-present rejection. No proof covers a genuine newly-created original=false artifact interrupted after staged.replace(live), and no proof challenges a forged original=true backup.
